threads.body: Catching OutOfMemoryError here can leave `garbage` with a very large backing buffer (StringBuilder retains capacity after `setLength(0)`), increasing memory pressure for the rest of the test run and potentially causing repeated OOMEs/timeouts. Consider shrinking the buffer when OOME occurs (e.g., call `trimToSize()` after clearing) or switching this temporary garbage generation to a local, throwaway allocation so memory can be reclaimed promptly.
The caught OutOfMemoryError is intentionally unused; per the repo catch-variable naming convention, please rename the catch parameter to `ignored` to make the intent explicit.
can we be smarter and not hit OOM? only because if we hit OOM it could cause other unrelated problems in the test harness

replies.body: It is the first test that triggers oom and only on jdk8. Could modify the test a bit to allocate less.
